narrative:
The model determined that you have a 25% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the total amount you wanted to borrow. 

Your very short six-month loan request actually worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward approval, as most approved applicants request loans lasting around 19 months. Unfortunately, this positive effect was outweighed by two negative factors. Having no checking account is relatively common among applicants but still pulled the decision toward higher risk. The loan amount of 3,518 DM also increased your risk score, as it sits noticeably above the average of about 3,020 DM requested by those who were approved.

Because the negative influences from your checking account status and requested amount were stronger than the positive effect of the short duration, the overall prediction tipped against approval.

You should consider reapplying with a smaller loan amount and opening a checking account first to demonstrate better financial visibility. These two changes would likely improve your chances significantly.
